title: Binary Search: Halving Your Way to the Answer
lead: Binary search finds a value in a sorted list by always cutting the search space in half. Instead of checking each element, you check the middle and discard the half where the answer cannot be.

sections.heading: The algorithm
sections.body: Start with low=0 and high=last index. Compute mid=(low+high)/2. If arr[mid] equals target — done. If target is smaller, move high to mid-1. If larger, move low to mid+1. Repeat until found or low > high. This is O(log N).

sections.heading: Why it needs sorted data
sections.body: The 'discard half' trick only works because in a sorted list you know the answer cannot be on the wrong side of mid. If the list is unsorted, binary search gives wrong answers. Always confirm sorted order first.

tryThis: Write the numbers 1 to 16 on paper. Find the number 11 using binary search — track how many comparisons you make. Compare that to checking one by one.
